report.source_text: The initial nephrology workup included a 24-h blood pressure monitor, serologic testing, urine sediment analysis, urinalysis, and kidney ultrasound. The 24-h blood pressure monitor revealed an average blood pressure of 126/80 mm Hg. The urinalysis results were remarkable for mild hematuria and proteinuria. The urine protein-creatinine ratio was 0.69 (reference range, less than 0.2), and the albumin-creatinine ratio was 22.4 mg/g (reference range, less than 30.0). A urine sediment analysis showed increased urinary B2-microglobulin of 359 mcg/L (reference range, less than 300 mcg/L). The serum creatinine had increased to 2.73 mg/dL from a baseline reading of 1.51 mg/dL, which was obtained 6 months prior. Due to the rapid decline in kidney function, a serologic workup for secondary causes of acute glomerulonephritis was performed. The results were inconclusive, however, with a positive ANA titer of 1: 640 and low complement 3 of 72.4 mg/ dL. The calcium level was in the reference range at 8.6 mg/dL. Serum and urine protein electrophoresis demonstrated a normal pattern. C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were normal at 0.2. The kidney ultrasound results were unremarkable.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old man with no prior hypertension history presented to ophthalmology in September 2019 with 1 month of bilateral blurry vision and glare. Initial examination revealed elevated intraocular pressures (33 mm Hg OD, 38 mm Hg OS) and fundus findings including mild optic nerve edema, scattered cotton-wool spots, retinal vessel congestion, and dot-blot hemorrhages, initially misattributed to hypertensive retinopathy. MRI brain was normal. Two months later, he developed vertical diplopia and right hypertropia (fourth cranial nerve palsy) with persistent cotton-wool spots, prompting referral to nephrology due to diagnostic discrepancies. Nephrology workup revealed rapid decline in renal function (creatinine increased from 1.51 to 2.73 mg/dL over 6 months), mild hematuria, proteinuria (urine protein-creatinine ratio 0.69), and elevated urinary B2-microglobulin (359 mcg/L). Renal biopsy demonstrated non-caseating granulomatous interstitial nephritis, negative for acid-fast bacilli and fungi. Serological testing showed elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) level of 73 U/L (reference <52 U/L), normal serum calcium (8.6 mg/dL), and normal CRP (0.2). Chest CT revealed a 4-mm partially calcified nodule in the left lower lobe, a 2.3-cm nodule in the right lung base, and non-specific mediastinal lymphadenopathy. The patient was started on oral prednisone 10 mg four times daily. Five months after treatment initiation, serum creatinine improved to 1.72 mg/dL (GFR improved from 24 to 40 mL/min), all neurologic symptoms resolved, and intraocular pressures normalized (15 mm Hg OD, 18 mm Hg OS).

final.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old man with no prior hypertension history presented to ophthalmology in September 2019 with 1 month of bilateral blurry vision and glare. Initial examination revealed elevated intraocular pressures (33 mm Hg OD, 38 mm Hg OS) and fundus findings including mild optic nerve edema, scattered cotton-wool spots, retinal vessel congestion, and dot-blot hemorrhages, initially misattributed to hypertensive retinopathy. MRI brain was normal. Two months later, he developed vertical diplopia and right hypertropia (fourth cranial nerve palsy) with persistent cotton-wool spots, prompting referral to nephrology due to diagnostic discrepancies. Nephrology workup revealed rapid decline in renal function (creatinine increased from 1.51 to 2.73 mg/dL over 6 months), mild hematuria, proteinuria (urine protein-creatinine ratio 0.69), and elevated urinary B2-microglobulin (359 mcg/L). Renal biopsy demonstrated non-caseating granulomatous interstitial nephritis, negative for acid-fast bacilli and fungi. Serological testing showed elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) level of 73 U/L (reference <52 U/L), normal serum calcium (8.6 mg/dL), and normal CRP (0.2). Chest CT revealed a 4-mm partially calcified nodule in the left lower lobe, a 2.3-cm nodule in the right lung base, and non-specific mediastinal lymphadenopathy. The patient was started on oral prednisone 10 mg four times daily. Five months after treatment initiation, serum creatinine improved to 1.72 mg/dL (GFR improved from 24 to 40 mL/min), all neurologic symptoms resolved, and intraocular pressures normalized (15 mm Hg OD, 18 mm Hg OS).
